title.narrative: Lifesaving response to worsening malnutrition, and disease outbreaks in most affected districts of Yemen

description.narrative: HealthThrough this project, WHO contributes to controlling outbreaks of cholera, diphtheria, measles, dengue, and other epidemic-prone diseases. Targeting 179,024 individuals across 14 districts in 9 governorates, the project employs an integrated health response to mitigate disease burdens, improve case management, and ultimately reduce morbidity and mortality associated with these diseases.Key Activities:Outbreak Alert Investigation and Detection:Equip 25 RRTs with essential supplies, enabling timely diagnosis and outbreak control in high-risk areas. Each team comprises five health workers and will conduct 318 field missions.Procure and distribute diagnostic testing kits to Central Public Health Laboratories in Sana’a and Aden for rapid identification of cholera, measles, diphtheria, and dengue.Improving Case Management:Provide refresher training for 75 healthcare workers on managing severe cases of communicable diseases to enhance early diagnosis and treatment.Distribute essential medicines, including antibiotics and IV fluids, to targeted health facilities in high-risk areas.Operationalize four DTCs for three months and establish ten additional centers as needed, informed by outbreak dynamics.Conduct regular supervisory visits (252 over six months) by WHO and MOH to monitor response activities.Procure emergency medical supplies to cover the needs of 140,000 individuals for IPC and WASH Practices:Improve WASH and IPC measures in 15 health facilities, including 4 DTCs, through the distribution of necessary supplies.Implement 28 hygiene promotion campaigns across 14 districts to raise awareness about disease prevention, complemented by 100,000 informational materials.Nutrition Under the nutrition sector, the project aims to reduce mortality and morbidity from acute malnutrition in children under five, particularly those facing multiple underlying causes such as childhood diseases, low immunization rates (53%), poor feeding practices, limited access to safe water, inadequate sanitation, and high food insecurity. In response to this critical situation, WHO is leading the provision of care for SAM/MC in inpatient settings across the country, especially in areas with IDPs Key Activities:Provision of operational support for the targeted TFCs: WHO is supporting 14 TFCs in targeted districts, with plans to expand services to an additional facility in Mawzaa, Taiz.Funding will cover performance-based service delivery costs for health workers (pediatricians, nurses, etc.), ensuring TFCs operate 24/7 and can effectively identify and treat children with malnutrition and related medical complications.Comprehensive Support Package:Provision of essential resources to TFCs, including clean water, meals for caregivers, cleaning supplies, laboratory tests, and stationery to maintain quality care.Free medication for all children treated in TFCs through the distribution of SAM/PED kits, ensuring comprehensive medical support for 50 cases per kit.Case Identification and Nutritional Assessment:Targeting a caseload of 5,692 children suffering from SAM/MC, WHO aims to enhance case identification by integrating nutritional assessments into various maternal and child health services across secondary health facilities.Expansion of routine nutrition sentinel sites (NSS) from 17 to 21 facilities in 15 districts, with a goal of assessing 30,000 children under five and 19,974 pregnant and lactating women (PLW) for malnutrition.Inpatient Case Management Training:Capacity-building for health workers on SAM/MC management to improve inpatient care quality, including procurement of necessary kitchenware for therapeutic milk preparation and WASH items to ensure infection control.Ongoing Technical Support and Supervision:WHO will conduct regular on-the-job mentoring and supervision to ensure adherence to operational guidelines in all supported TFCs, including training on identifying and referring women in need of MHPSS.
